clue.text: Runs through fence on motorway when reversing

indicators.note: in this clue the fence is set on, that is after, the turned motorway
says the motorway's letters are turned round to read the other way

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's best-known motorway, written MI
pales are pointed stakes forming a fence

explanation.surface: Someone describes a car crashing through a fence while reversing on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main motorway; motorway in crosswords often gives M or MI. In an across clue 'on' here means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce or run a sharp point through something, so a straight synonym.

clue.text: Dope — taking in line, with this smooth entry?

indicators.note: the dope's letters take the line inside them

parts.note: dope is slang for information

explanation.surface: A drug addict asks whether snorting a line gives a smooth hit.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflow is a flowing in, a smooth entry of liquid or air.

clue.text: Crack: troop in charge covered entrance

indicators.note: crack means break up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: An elite troop guards a covered entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like an adjective, elite, describing the troop, but it is the anagram signal applied to TROOP plus IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch with a roof supported by columns, a covered entrance to a building.

clue.text: Recurrent theme resulting from tie to film

indicators.note: the answer results from reshaping these words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recurring theme springs from a link to a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a recurrent musical or literary theme associated with a character or idea.

clue.text: Ceremonial officer shortly has information on native servant

parts.note: has shortened gives 's
word means news or information
a bearer was a native servant or porter in colonial India

explanation.surface: A ceremonial official briefly receives news about a local servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordbearer is an official who carries a ceremonial sword before a mayor or monarch.

clue.text: Minor personalities touring eastern island

indicators.note: going round, so the celebrities' letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: celebs, short for celebrities, often minor ones

explanation.surface: Minor celebrities on a tour of an island in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebes, now usually called Sulawesi, is a large Indonesian island: a specific example.

clue.text: The function of officers'

definitions.meaning: belonging to commanding officers, abbreviated with an apostrophe

explanation.definitionFit: Cos is short for cosine, a trigonometric function, and COs' means belonging to commanding officers.

clue.text: See perennial partly curl up inside

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Look at a perennial plant partly curling up inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'See 'perennial' as the definition from an OCR stray apostrophe; the page prints 'See perennial', and only 'perennial' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a perennial garden plant with tall spikes of flowers, an example of the class.

clue.text: Vamoose shortly to Iowa — what a bloomer

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: vamoose is slang for go away, begone
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

explanation.surface: Someone told to clear off to Iowa makes a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: BEGONE cut short loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: A begonia is a flowering plant, a bloomer, while a bloomer also means a blunder.

clue.text: Unscrupulous people get pension scheme to cover medical speciality

indicators.note: the pension scheme's letters go over the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: SERPS was Britain's State Earnings-Related Pension Scheme
ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine

explanation.surface: Crooks are drawn by a pension plan covering specialist medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: SERPS, the State Earnings-Related Pension Scheme, ran in Britain from 1978.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpents figuratively are treacherous or sly people, as in a snake in the grass.

clue.text: They are kept on the hearth, next to the dogs

definitions.text: They are kept on the hearth, next to the dogs

parts.words: They are kept on the hearth, next to the dogs
parts.note: the dogs are firedogs, the metal supports for logs in a fireplace, not pets curled up by the fire; the tools beside them are the poker, tongs and shovel

explanation.surface: Something kept by the fireside next to the family's pet dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire irons are the poker, tongs and shovel kept beside the andirons (firedogs) on a hearth.

clue.text: Long time to get pair round? This may summon one

indicators.note: the pair's letters go round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Getting a couple to come round takes ages; perhaps a bleeper would call them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager is a bleeper used to summon someone such as a doctor on call.

clue.text: Open University Marxist leader embracing smug people's religion

indicators.note: the Open University letters hug the rest, holding them inside

parts.note: OU is the abbreviation for Britain's Open University
pi is informal British for sanctimonious or smugly pious

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of Marxist is taken

explanation.surface: A Marxist lecturer at the Open University hugging complacent folk.
explanation.walkthrough: Marx called religion the opium of the people, so the definition reverses his phrase; 'Marxist' in the surface points straight at the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx famously described religion as the opium of the people, so the drug stands for their religion.

clue.text: Holding free trip to make reparation

indicators.note: the trip's letters hold the other piece inside them

parts.note: to trip, as in trip the light fantastic, is to dance
open means free or available

explanation.surface: A free trip is offered as compensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing penance means performing an act of atonement to make up for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Scheme to try to get off with

definitions.meaning: a plan or proposal put forward
make a sexual advance to someone

explanation.definitionFit: A proposition is a proposed plan, and to proposition someone is to make them a sexual offer.

clue.text: The top arts form is ill-disciplined usually

indicators.note: the words are out of order, unruly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Top art forms are said to be undisciplined.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means mostly or in general, a set expression synonymous with usually.

clue.text: Indian tax collector lifting lid on raids designed to catch fifty.

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: the rearranged letters catch the other piece inside them
designed, as in remodelled, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An Indian tax official lifts the lid on raids planned to snare fifty people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns HAT up into TAH; 'designed' rearranges RAIDS as SIDAR, which catches L.
explanation.definitionFit: A tahsildar is a revenue officer in charge of a tahsil, a district subdivision in India.

clue.text: For example, say why Scotsman receives exercises in Arabic

indicators.note: say signals a sound-alike: the word is spoken, giving a letter

parts.note: spoken, why is the letter Y
PT is physical training
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name; he receives the exercises placed just before him

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why a Scot takes exercises in Arabic.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptian Arabic is the dialect spoken in Egypt, so the word can describe Arabic of that land.

clue.text: Black sheep is eatable at no cost

parts.note: food that is eatable is good, not gone off
for nothing means free of charge

explanation.surface: Someone claims a black sheep is fine to eat and costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black sheep' looks like an animal ready for the table, but it is the family disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A black sheep is the disreputable member of a family, a ne'er-do-well or wastrel.

clue.text: Ishmael found unconscious at first

indicators.note: the unconscious piece goes first, before the other

parts.note: out cold, so out
to found metal is to cast it

explanation.surface: Ishmael was discovered unconscious at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Ishmael, son of Abraham and Hagar, was cast out into the desert, as was the narrator of Moby-Dick in spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishmael in Genesis was banished with his mother, so his name means an exile or pariah.

clue.text: Egg has to be worth salt

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
rate means merit or be worth, as in rate a mention

explanation.surface: An egg must be worth its salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a salt of nitric acid, an example of the chemical class.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill capturing Maine in satirical play

indicators.note: the outer name captures the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: Buffalo Bill was William Cody, the US showman
ME is the abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: Buffalo Bill seizes Maine in a satirical stage piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy is a humorous play, and satire is one of its forms.

clue.text: Selection of tunes in medley may be up to Prior

indicators.note: words mixed in a medley may be shuffled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical selection performed as a medley might be left to Prior to choose.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a mixture, and in music a medley or selection of tunes.

clue.text: Month on a lake based on eights

parts.note: Oct is short for October

explanation.surface: A month spent by a lake follows a pattern of eights.
explanation.definitionFit: Octal describes the base-8 number system, counting in groups of eight.

clue.text: Preliminary section; it's not at the end of the anthem

indicators.note: the two letters of 'it' are missing from the close of the other word

parts.note: an introit is an anthem or psalm sung as the priest approaches the altar
the word it, its letters taken out

explanation.surface: Someone notes a part missing at the close of the national anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: INTROIT, a church anthem, loses its final IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the preliminary section of a piece of music or writing.

clue.text: Not suitable as part of Advanced Passenger Train

parts.note: being in something is being part of it
APT was the British Rail tilting train of the 1980s

explanation.surface: Something deemed unsuitable to form part of the Advanced Passenger Train.
explanation.walkthrough: The APT was British Rail's experimental tilting express, withdrawn after problems: an apt target for the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Not a steady sort of meeting

definitions.text: Not a steady sort of meeting

parts.words: Not a steady sort of meeting
parts.note: a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend; this rendezvous is with a stranger set up by friends, not an unsteady one

explanation.surface: A gathering described as wobbly or irregular.
explanation.definitionFit: A date arranged between strangers who have never met, so not with one's steady partner.

clue.text: Person losing diamonds from corsage

indicators.note: the dress part loses some letters, which are taken away

parts.note: a corsage is the bodice of a dress
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone loses the diamonds pinned to their corsage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bod is informal British for a person or body, as in an odd bod.

clue.text: Irritated after tax took precedence

parts.note: nett, or net, describes a sum after tax is deducted
led means went first or took precedence

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed that tax was put first.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettled means annoyed or irritated, as if stung by nettles.

clue.text: Attend carefully to the lines in this sort of rhyme

parts.note: to nurse is to tend or look after carefully
RY, short for railway, as railway lines

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay close attention to the lines of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like verse but is the railway, RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery rhymes are traditional verses for small children, so the word names this type of rhyme.
